findings.quote: the FY23 figures predate two years of losses and negative free cash flow that would have drawn on the balance sheet
findings.issue: "Two years of losses" (FY24 and FY25) is contradicted by the income statement on the same page: FY24 operating income was +$1.2B and FY24 net income +$1.1B (+$1.57 diluted EPS) — FY24 was profitable, not a loss year. Only FY25 was a net/operating loss. The same error recurs at sections.risks.idiosyncratic[3]: "current leverage and net-debt/EBITDA cannot be verified from this report after two loss-making years." (FY24 did have marginally negative FCF of -$26M, but that is negative cash flow, not a loss.) The mischaracterization overstates the depth and duration of the downturn.
findings.fix: Recast to what the surface supports: FY23 total/net debt predate FY24-FY25 of weak-to-negative free cash flow (FY24 roughly breakeven at -$26M, FY25 -$1.4B) and the FY25 net loss. Do not call FY24 a loss year. Apply the same correction to the idiosyncratic-risk bullet ("after a loss-making FY25 and two years of negative free cash flow").
findings.note: Still resolved in the republish. The FY23-predates passage is gone because the corrected pack now carries FY24 and FY25 debt. No "two years of losses" or "two loss-making years" wording remains, and FY24 is described as "roughly breakeven" free cash flow.

findings.quote: the shares retest toward the 52-week low of $20.65, about 23% below the $28.65 price

findings.fix: Attach the 23% to the $22 bear implied price, e.g. "the shares retest toward the 52-week low of $20.65; our $22 bear case is about 23% below the $28.65 price," so the percentage matches the calls math.
findings.note: Superseded. The Bear is now $20.65, the 52-week low itself, and the page's -27.9% bear-case downside matches (1 - 20.65/28.65 = 27.9%). No 23% figure remains anywhere in the judgment.

findings.quote: For an industrial company that zone caps the published label at HOLD, whatever the scenarios derive.
findings.issue: The gate does not cap the published label. scripts/synth-build.ts calls decide() with SAFE_DEFAULTS (enforceGate false). Even with enforcement on, decide() caps only at high gate confidence, and gates.ts sets confidence to low for any WEAK zone. The HOLD ceiling is stored as rating.gate.gatedLabel and is advisory: an earlier build of this draft printed "gate ceiling HOLD (weak-balance-sheet) — advisory, not applied" against a composed BUY. So finalRecommendation.body[1] is wrong on the page's math: at $26 the scenarios derive BUY (E +12.0%, R 0.58x), and BUY could be published. The lift condition is also misstated. WEAK clears when coverage reaches 1x and leverage falls to 6x, not when coverage "turns positive". The rest of the gate explanation is accurate (see F-9 for DISTRESS). The cap claim appears four times: here; analystCommentary ("caps the label at HOLD"); finalRecommendation.body[0] ("would cap the label at HOLD in any case"); and body[1] ("the gate would still hold the label at HOLD until trailing interest coverage turns positive and leverage falls; an upgrade needs both"). Catalysts[2] ("turn positive and begin to lift the WEAK gate") carries the same threshold error.
findings.fix: Explain the gate once, here. It sets an advisory HOLD ceiling and marks the balance sheet as too weak to support a buy-side call, but it does not change the published label, which follows the scenarios. In analystCommentary and body[0], drop the cap wording and keep "the scenarios derive HOLD on their own". In body[1], say the scenarios would derive BUY at or below the target low and the WEAK gate would remain a reason for caution until trailing earnings cover interest and leverage falls back. Do not present "an upgrade needs both" as a rule. In catalysts[2], replace "turn positive" with "recover enough to cover interest", without adding a number.
findings.note: Resolved. Every claim that the gate caps the label is gone. balanceCommentary now explains the gate once: an advisory HOLD ceiling that the portfolio acts on, with the published label following the scenarios. That matches synth-build (SAFE_DEFAULTS) and eligibility.ts. finalRecommendation.body[1] now says a price at or below the target low derives BUY (correct: E +12.0%, R 0.58x). catalysts[2] says earnings "recover enough to cover interest".

findings.quote: We reject that: the market already pays more than that for FY27E today, and no source supports a de-rating.
findings.issue: The rejection uses the basis that docs/10022026learning.md section 13 (USFD F-15) rules out. When the Base values the shares a year out on FY27E, today's forward multiple (12.0x, a current-year multiple on FY26E) is the like-for-like reference. A year out, FY27 is the current year, so 16.1x on it raises the current-year multiple from 12.0x. That makes 12.0x the held multiple, not a de-rating. multiplesCommentary makes the same inversion: "so that FY27E multiple is the like-for-like reference" and "because we hold today's multiple rather than assume a higher one". The rejection is also circular: the market pays 16.1x for FY27 today because FY27 is a year further out. Both robustness claims hold on the page's math. A Street-median Base ($34.00) gives E +10.9% and R 0.39x, so HOLD. A 12.0x Base ($21.36) gives E -11.1%, so SELL. Shifting ten points of weight gives +7.8% or -4.6%. But a Base below about $24.87 (about 14.0x FY27E) derives SELL, so a basis midway between the two multiples sits at the line. "The Street's median target reflects that view" gives analysts a rationale that no source states.
findings.fix: Drop "like-for-like reference", "de-rating" and "rather than assume a higher one". Say the Base assumes that a year out the market pays the multiple it pays for FY27 today, which is above today's current-year multiple. Argue that from both sides with the reasons already on the page. Say that holding today's current-year multiple derives SELL, that a basis between the two sits near the SELL line, and so the call is close to SELL. Write "is consistent with that view" instead of "reflects". HOLD can stand if it is argued this way. This is not a request to change the label.
findings.note: Resolved. The Base is now described as raising today’s 12.0x current-year multiple and is argued from both sides; "like-for-like" and "de-rating" are gone. The report says the call is close to SELL and that a basis halfway between the two multiples sits at the SELL line (14.05x gives $25.01, E -4.8%; correct). "is consistent with that view" replaces "reflects". Scenarios are unchanged.

findings.quote: the Alberta net-zero cracker project is meant to extend the cost and emissions position
findings.issue: The 10-K excerpt calls the Alberta facility "a key element for the Company to achieve its 2030 greenhouse gas emissions reduction commitment". No source says it is meant to extend the cost position. That purpose is the author's inference, and it supports the moat argument the paragraph is making.
findings.fix: Tie the project to what the 10-K says, e.g. "the Alberta net-zero cracker project is meant to deliver the company's 2030 emissions-reduction commitment, though the 10-K lists its cost and timing among the risks". Drop "cost" as a stated purpose.
findings.note: Resolved. durability now follows the 10-K: the project is "a key element in achieving the company’s 2030 greenhouse gas emissions reduction commitment", and its cost and timing are listed among the risks. The cost-position purpose is gone.

findings.quote: Near-term liquidity is adequate. The current ratio was 1.97 at FY25 and 1.75 on trailing figures, and the gate does not read DISTRESS.
findings.issue: The sentence reads as though the current ratio keeps the gate out of DISTRESS. In gates.ts the current-ratio test reads DISTRESS only when the ratio is below 1 and there is under a year of cash, so it is not close. The near test is coverage: a net debtor with coverage under 1x reads DISTRESS if cash covers under two years of negative FCF. Dow meets two of its three conditions. It misses DISTRESS only because FY25 cash and investments ($3.8B) cover about 2.7 years of FY25's -$1.4B free cash flow. That is the cushion to watch.
findings.fix: Add in words that FY25 cash and short-term investments cover the FY25 free-cash-flow shortfall more than twice over, which keeps the gate out of DISTRESS. Keep the current-ratio sentence as context. Add no new number.
findings.note: Resolved. balanceCommentary now says the gate does not read DISTRESS because FY25 cash and short-term investments covered the FY25 free-cash-flow shortfall more than twice over (3.8/1.4, about 2.7 years, against the two-year test). It also says what would turn the zone to DISTRESS. The current ratio is kept as context.
